item.title: Exit Tickets
item.description:
Exit Tickets

A short in-class response that closes each meeting. Credit-based, low-stakes, one for every class day (42 across the semester).

Exit tickets do double duty: they tell your instructor what landed and what didn’t before the next class, and they give you a running record of your own thinking to draw on when you write your weekly forum post.

Format

  • Short, in-class, low-stakes
  • Credit-based (completion, not correctness)

Rhythm

  • Every class day

Submission

  • Completed in class
  • (TODO) Confirm whether tickets are submitted on D2L or another in-class mechanism

📌 See the syllabus for how Exit Tickets factor into your Class Engagement grade.

item.title: Forum Posts
item.description:
Forum Posts

Each week there’s outside material to read, watch, or listen to. You respond to a posed question about that material in a roughly 250-word post, using evidence from the material (and your own research) with APA formatting. This is also the main place you’ll do the metacognitive analysis described in the learning goals — how your own use of and relationship to these systems is shifting.

Replying to classmates’ posts (Forum Replies) is a deeper-engagement option: same evidence-and-citation expectations as the original post, civil and grounded in documentable research.

item.title: Case Studies
item.description:
Case Studies

Most weeks begin with a particular use case of AI in society, presented by the instructor. In class, your group (3–4 students) analyzes the case using the DTPA framework, answering key questions with evidence. Early on, groups focus on one component of DTPA at a time (Data, then Tools, then Practices); later, groups apply the full framework and are expected to find additional cases in the same area (e.g., voting, criminal justice, the environment) to synthesize across uses.

item.title: Lesson Planning & Leading Class
item.description:
Lesson Planning & Leading Class

After the first few weeks of class, groups of students (3–4) can opt in to plan and lead a lesson. Expect this to take each student roughly 10 hours to plan and lead. This is a deeper engagement option, not a requirement.

How to sign up

  • Reach out to your instructor at least one week before your planned lesson
  • A student may only participate once
  • Scheduling depends on availability — your lesson may land later in the semester than requested

What’s expected

  • Learning goals for the session
  • Engagement strategies
  • An appropriate Exit Ticket for your lesson

📌 See the syllabus for how leading a class factors into your Class Engagement grade.

item.title: Case Design
item.description:
Case Design

The principal assessment for the course: a semester-long, scaffolded case design project completed in teams of 3–4. Your chosen topic must be substantial enough in scope to warrant a group effort.

Guided by the DTPA framework, your team develops one of two kinds of case:

I. Proactive AI Solution — a proposed AI application that directly addresses a societal issue while maintaining transparency around its biases, ethical boundaries, and real-world impact on communities.
